title: Man-Marking a Key Opponent
content: Man-marking assigns one defender the primary responsibility of following a specific opponent wherever they move on the pitch, regardless of positional shape. This is typically deployed against a single opponent who is the creative hub of the opposition — a playmaker, a false 9, or a technically exceptional player. The marker's job is to deny that player time and space, forcing the opponent to use other (presumably lesser) players. Key requirements: the marker must have the physical and mental stamina to maintain the press for 90 minutes, excellent positional awareness to stay goal-side while tracking movement, and composure to not be drawn into dangerous positions by decoy runs. Risk: man-marking can pull defenders out of position, creating space for other attackers.
